director.chapterArc: Intake at Meridian Station: A transition from survival horror to bureaucratic reality. The scene moves through three distinct phases: arrival (mystery), medical processing (clinical detachment and shock of unconditional care), and registration (the revelation of Toren's 'nought' status, Rook's anomaly, and the conditional nature of their stay). The emotional core is the group's shared silence regarding Milo Faust and Toren's lost power.
director.restraintNote: Maintain a grounded, observational tone. Avoid melodrama in the medical scenes; let the clinical descriptions carry the weight. When characters speak (Nesbitt, Ambrose), keep their voices flat and factual to contrast with the internal turmoil of the group. Do not rush the silence after Toren's 'nought' reading or Rook's bench failure.

cues.delivery: Start with a grounded, observational tone. The sound is described as 'not of the world'; keep it low and even without rising inflection.
cues.from: Meridian came out to get them, and the sound it came out with was the worst thing that happened to Toren Voss all day.
cues.through: It was low. It was even. It did not vary.

cues.delivery: Toren's whisper of 'Milo' should be internalized and quiet. Do not make it a sob; treat it as a factual acknowledgment of absence.
cues.from: "Milo," he said, out loud, in the ash.
cues.through: "I know," said Dessa. "He'd have gone and got in it."

cues.delivery: Nesbitt's dialogue must be delivered with clinical precision. No rising inflection for questions; treat the 'compliment' as a statement of fact about her unusual behavior.
cues.from: "Right. Don't sit up, don't be helpful, don't tell me you can walk." She crouched at six feet. "My name's Nesbitt and I'm the south warden. This is the first time I have ever come out of my own gate for anybody, so you can take that as either a compliment or a piece of information about how the day's going. Is there anybody else on this ground?"
cues.through: "Everything else here is a great deal more complicated than you are going to like. That isn't."
cues.reason: Character differentiation: Nesbitt is authoritative but gentle.

cues.delivery: Toren's admission of his broken arm and lost Ember. Delivered with exhaustion and a desire to delay the pain.
cues.from: "My arm's broken and the Ember's out," said Toren, "and I don't know how to say either of those and I'd like not to yet."
cues.through: "Right," he said. "Then we'll do it later. I'll be on this bench."

cues.delivery: The description of the lamp. Keep it factual and observational; do not sound awestruck.
cues.from: That was the thing. He lay on a table with his left forearm out on a board and a woman of about forty putting her thumbs where they had to go, and above him, screwed to the ceiling, there was a glass tube the length of his arm that was full of light.
cues.through: Afterward, with the arm in a splint and the whole of him grey, he lay on a bed in a room with four beds in it and looked at the ceiling.

cues.delivery: Toren's internal realization that his Ember is gone. The dialogue with Dessa should be sparse and quiet.
cues.through: "Not yet." He did not look at her. "Not today. Everybody in this place has got one thing left in them and they've all spent it. If I say it out loud today, then Rook has to get up off whatever they've put him on. And he will. And he cannot."
cues.reason: Subtext: Shared burden of the secret.

cues.delivery: Rook's declaration 'One line' and his name reveal. Keep Rook's voice flat and declarative; the tension comes from what is *not* said.
cues.from: Rook was in the second chair with his shoulder dressed and his left forearm dressed under it and his face the colour of the wall.
cues.reason: Character differentiation: Rook speaks with low reserve.

cues.delivery: Purdy reading the ledger. The delivery should be completely ordinary; the horror is in the content.
cues.from: "Marsh, E.," Purdy read out, in a completely ordinary voice, because it was a completely ordinary line in a book. "Nineteen. Party of ten off the south road. Conditional, reviewed, cleared the fourth of the twelfth. And there's a second hand under it, later, in pencil." He looked up. "Went out again on his own in the spring. Would not take the allocation."
cues.through: "So you're already a line," said Purdy, and turned the book back round. "That makes this considerably shorter. Thank you."
cues.reason: Contrast: Bureaucratic tone vs. dramatic revelation.

cues.delivery: Dessa and Wyck's readings. Keep the pacing steady; do not rush to the result.
cues.from: Dessa went first, because Dessa always went first when a thing was unpleasant and unavoidable.
cues.through: Wyck went second and read two, which made him blink.

cues.delivery: Toren's 'nought' reading. The narration should slow slightly to let the silence of the needle land.
cues.through: "He's a nought on my bench today and that's all my bench does." Sowerby did not look up. "If it's different next year it'll say different next year. Next."

cues.delivery: Toren's internal monologue about Milo. Keep it analytical and distant.
cues.from: Toren sat down on a chair in a corridor at Meridian with a card in his hand that said Kindled on it in a clerk's handwriting.
cues.through: Nobody said one word to Toren about that card, then or ever.

cues.delivery: Rook's bench reading. The narration should be precise; the sound of the needle hitting the pin is a physical event.
cues.from: They put Rook on the bench last.
cues.through: Then he came back and sat down and wrote in his notebook for about four minutes without saying anything at all.
cues.reason: Dramatic landing: Rook is an anomaly.

cues.delivery: Ambrose's exposition. Delivered with professional coldness but underlying empathy; no rising inflection for the 'four things'.
cues.from: Registrar Ambrose came at half past seven. She was not unkind, and that was the whole difficulty.
cues.through: "Get some sleep," she said. "Somebody will bring you bread at nine."
cues.reason: Character differentiation: Ambrose is precise and rhythmic.

cues.delivery: The bread distribution. Keep the rhythm steady; 'Milo' should be a quiet acknowledgment.
cues.from: Dessa took it out and put it on the cloth and got the small knife out of her coat — not the station's knife, her own, the one she had been cutting with since the platform — and cut it into six, poorly, which was not an accident.
cues.through: And Elias Marsh got up off a chair in the south quarter of a tech-zone station with his shoulder dressed and his name in a book from eleven years ago, and came and took it out of her hand, and ate the whole of it standing up, because a boy had told her to make him.

pauses.reason: Emphasis on the uncanny nature of the arrival.

pauses.after: It was low. It was even. It did not vary.

pauses.reason: Isolating the name as a pivotal emotional anchor.

pauses.after: "I know," said Dessa. "He'd have gone and got in it."

pauses.reason: Emphasis on the specific threat classification.

pauses.after: And then he was inside, and he could not see any of it, because he was on his back.

pauses.reason: Highlighting the mundane miracle of abundance.

pauses.after: Toren Voss, who had carried water in two cans across a dying country, went past that yard on a stretcher with a broken arm and cried so hard that one of the bearers stopped and had to be told to keep going.
"Everything else here is a great deal more complicated than you are going to like. That isn't."

pauses.reason: Emphasis on the unnatural nature of the lamp.

pauses.after: Toren went in after the warmth about nine times in the first hour and every single time he came back with nothing at all. Not a flicker. Not a cold seam in a bed of ash waiting for a handful of thorn. There was no seam. There was a place under his breastbone, low and central and slightly behind, that he had known about since the evening he was thirteen, and there was nothing in it.

pauses.reason: Isolating the question about his power level.

pauses.after: "All right," she said. "Then I'll carry it with you and I won't say it to anybody. And I want that logged as a thing I am doing on purpose and not a thing I forgot."

"Marsh, E.," Purdy read out, in a completely ordinary voice, because it was a completely ordinary line in a book. "Nineteen. Party of ten off the south road. Conditional, reviewed, cleared the fourth of the twelfth. And there's a second hand under it, later, in pencil." He looked up. "Went out again on his own in the spring. Would not take the allocation."

pauses.reason: Emphasis on the name reveal and its weight.

pauses.after: Nobody said one word to Toren about that card, then or ever.

pauses.reason: Emphasis on Rook's anomaly being confirmed as a physical state.
Emphasis on Ambrose's personal concession to the group.

pauses.after: She put the folder under her arm.
